credentials.description: service ID — the user part of HTTP Basic auth, base64(SERVICE_ID:SECRET_TOKEN)
secret token — the password part of HTTP Basic auth

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Verification identifier returned by send_verification (verificationid field).

example_prompt: Verify the OTP my user entered during phone verification.

code.description: Code entered by the user (integer, 4 to 6 digits depending on code_length). Send as an integer, not as a string.

status.description: Verification status after the attempt. 'approved' = correct code. 'too_many_attemps' = attempts exhausted (typo in the API, a single 't' in 'attempts').

gotchas: The 'code' field is an integer (not a string). Send the code entered by the user as an integer in the JSON body.
The 'id' field in the URL corresponds to the 'verificationid' field (not 'id') returned by send_verification.
The 'too_many_attemps' status (with a single letter 't' in 'attempts') is a typo in the NimbaSMS API — handle this exact value in the code.
Each wrong call decrements the attempt counter. Once exhausted (status: 'too_many_attemps'), the verification expires — create a new one via send_verification.
Never call this endpoint client-side — call it only server-side with the code entered by the user. An 'approved' status must immediately mark the number as verified in the database.
open_questions: Sandbox: provider.json declares none and no gotcha documents a test environment — every call reaches production.
